decisions.rationale: Down 0-1, need speed control. Whimsicott+Incineroar lead with Tailwind setup and Intimidate pivot. Backline Garchomp Scarf handles Dragapult, Manectric provides Electric coverage. Lucario-Mega needs Tailwind to outspeed Dragapult Scarf. Incineroar Protect streak risky but Intimidate valuable.
decisions.notebook: Dragapult Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Darts. Rotom pivots with VoltSwitch and uses Will-O-Wisp frequently. Gholdengo is target for Earthquake but can switch to Rotom. Grimmsnarl Prankster threat. Lucario-Mega requires Tailwind to outspeed Dragapult Scarf. Incineroar Protect streak is risky. Whimsicott Timid 184 Speed + Prankster Tailwind essential. Garchomp Scarf 136 Speed handles Dragapult 161-213 if Tailwind active.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl + Rotom press early: Fake Out + Will-O-Wisp disrupts the scarf/garchomp tempo. Floette-Eternal Mega (Floettite) provides speed and status support; Gholdengo drives momentum with typing and coverage. This covers Garchomp-Lucario core, counters Tailwind windows, and preserves backline flexibility.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Garchomp + Mega Lucario core; scarf Garchomp outspeeds non-scarf threats; Whimsicott Tailwind to boost tempo; Protect to stall with Lucario. Revealed: Mega Lucario arrived and was KO'd; Dragapult with Scarf ended up locked into DragonDarts on critical turns. Future plan: counter scarf Garchomp with a fast, non-locking check when possible, rely on Rotom's Will-O-Wisp to blunt Garchomp, while using Grimmsnarl's Fake Out and Floette-Eternal Mega for speed and protection; Gholdengo as momentum driver.

decisions.rationale: Secure Tailwind for Dragapult speed control. Incineroar FakeOut flinches Grimmsnarl, shutting down Prankster. Whimsicott Focus Sash survives Grimmsnarl FakeOut if it moves first.
decisions.notebook: Dragapult Scarf is primary threat; Tailwind mandatory for Garchomp/Manectric. Grimmsnarl Prankster FakeOut is immediate danger. Whimsicott Focus Sash guarantees survival. Incineroar Intimidate lowers Grimmsnarl Atk. Rotom pivots with VoltSwitch. Gholdengo target for Earthquake. Floette-Eternal Mega threat. Absol Focus Sash revenge killer.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl plus Rotom create tempo deny and threat mitigation: Fake Out stops Whimsicott's Tailwind this turn; Will-O-Wisp on Incineroar weakens its physical presence for the next exchanges, enabling our faster pivots and momentum for Gholdengo/Floette-Eternal.
decisions.notebook: Intended Mega: Lucario-Mega. Other Mega Stone holders should be evaluated in base forme (Floette-Eternal with Floettite). Opening aims: disrupt Whimsicott's Tailwind with Fake Out, blunt Incineroar's physicals with Will-O-Wisp, and build tempo for Gholdengo and Floette-Eternal. Opponent tendencies to watch: scarf Garchomp outspeed risk, Protect stalls with Lucario, and continued tempo from Whimsicott. Adapt Mega choice and switches based on opponent's set in game 3.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind enables Garchomp/Manectric for late game. Incineroar Protect avoids Rotom Hex (super effective on Dark) and Grimmsnarl Brick Break (super effective on Dark). Focus Sash Whimsicott survives any hit. Protecting Incineroar is safer than attacking given its low Speed and type disadvantage.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Rotom)
decisions.rationale: Prioritize defensive supports (Light Screen) to cushion special attackers while continuing pressure on Whimsicott with Will-O-Wisp to blunt its offensive presence and preserve tempo for Gholdengo/Floette-Eternal.
decisions.notebook: Strategy: Mega Lucario remains the planned centerpiece for late-game, but evaluate other Mega-Stone holdings (Floette-Eternal with Floettite) in base form for game 3. Turn 2 aims: disable Whimsicott's Tailwind threat and blunt Incineroar's physicals via Will-O-Wisp, then build tempo for our backline (Gholdengo/Floette-Eternal). Watch for scarf Garchomp and Lucario Protect tendencies; adjust Megas and switches accordingly in game 3.

decisions.rationale: Encore Grimmsnarl locks it into Light Screen (last move), preventing Brick Break. Incineroar Flare Blitz deals heavy damage to Grimmsnarl. Grimmsnarl is the immediate threat; locking it removes pressure while Whimsicott Focus Sash ensures survival. Protect is safe but less aggressive.

Turn 3 plan: switch Grimmsnarl to Gholdengo to preserve screens and gain Good as Gold immunity to status; Rotom uses Will-O-Wisp into Incineroar (4) to blunt physical threat and enable Hex later; Lucario remains the intended Mega centerpiece for game 3; avoid switching Floette-Eternal now to keep Lucario Mega as primary.
decisions.notebook: Intended Mega: Lucario; Floette-Eternal remains in base form (Floettite held but not Mega). Plan: bring in Gholdengo to enforce status-immunity and keep Lights/Reflect up; Rotom to burn Incineroar to blunt physicals and set up Hex; monitor Tailwind and opposing backline (Garchomp/Lucario/Krookodile) to time Mega Lucario for late-game pressure; adapt in game 3 if opponent pivots to different Mega; maintain tempo to reach 2-1 in the series.

decisions.rationale: Switching Gholdengo to Grimmsnarl preserves dual-screen support (Reflect) while enabling Brick Break to pressure and potentially remove opponent screens; Rotom passes to keep Will-O-Wisp timing intact and avoid overextending before the switch resolves.
decisions.notebook: Intended Mega: Lucario. Floette-Eternal remains non-Mega with Floettite. Plan: reestablish dual screens (Light Screen from Grimmsnarl + Reflect), pressure the backline with Brick Break, and use Rotom’s Will-O-Wisp to blunt Incineroar when possible. Monitor Tailwind and save Gholdengo’s status-immunity for when it can re-enter (or when it’s safe to pivot into a Gholdengo re-entry). Time Mega Lucario to spike pressure in the late game and swing momentum to p1 if turnout allows. Prepare for Game 3 adjustments if Whimsicott’s Encore persists.

decisions.rationale: Lock Rotom into Will-O-Wisp (useless on Fire/Whimsicott) to prevent pivoting. Protect Incineroar from Grimmsnarl's super-effective Brick Break. Maintain Tailwind for sweepers.

Plan: maintain dual screens, pressure backline, and chip Incineroar with Will-O-Wisp; wait for Tailwind to fade and execute Mega Lucario sweep in late game. Monitor Encore on Gholdengo and adjust switches accordingly.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl is the immediate threat to Incineroar. Moonblast (2x) + Parting Shot (Atk down) maximizes damage and safety. Rotom is Encored and harmless. Tailwind expires next turn, but Grimmsnarl must be removed first.

Whimsicott Protects to survive Floette's Moonblast with Focus Sash backup. Manectric switches in faster than Garchomp (139 vs 136), hits Rotom with STAB Thunderbolt, and maintains Tailwind speed advantage. Incineroar must switch per menu options.

Switch Grimmsnarl to Floette-Eternal to preserve dual screens for Lucario's late-game Mega sweep; have Rotom target Incineroar with Will-O-Wisp to blunt its physical power while Rotom remains Encore-locked. This keeps pressure on backline and minimizes risk of a free Lucario setup turn as Tailwind fades.
decisions.notebook: Intended Mega: Lucario. Floette-Eternal retained as non-Mega with Floettite. Plan: maintain dual screens, pressure backline, and chip Incineroar with Will-O-Wisp; wait for Tailwind to fade and execute Mega Lucario sweep in late game. Monitor Encore on Rotom and adjust switches accordingly. If Rotom's Encore persists, adapt by guiding Floette-Eternal into safer roles and preserving Lucario's mega window.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott Encore locks Floette into Moonblast, preventing Mega Evolution which is critical. Whimsicott is faster and survives the locked Moonblast due to Floette's -1 SpA. Manectric Thunderbolt chips Floette safely as it cannot attack back. Rotom is locked into Will-O-Wisp and poses minimal threat.
decisions.notebook: Dragapult Scarf is primary late-game threat. Grimmsnarl Prankster FakeOut used. Whimsicott Focus Sash only works at full HP. Rotom Encored into Will-O-Wisp (volatile). Floette-Eternal holds Floettite; preventing Mega is priority. Tailwind expired Turn 5. Whimsicott HP 66% brn, vulnerable. Manectric HP 94% brn. Incineroar Intimidate active. Garchomp Scarf available for Dragapult. Absol Focus Sash revenge killer.

decisions.rationale: KO Whimsicott with Moonblast to remove its support; switching Rotom to Grimmsnarl breaks the current Encore lock and brings in a bulky pivot while preserving Lucario Mega timing. This keeps dual-screen pressure and empowers a late-game Lucario Mega sweep.
decisions.notebook: Intended Mega: Lucario. Floette-Eternal remains non-Mega with Floettite. Turn 6 aims to KO Whimsicott and remove Rotom’s Encore threat by switching Rotom out. Maintain dual screens (Light Screen/Reflect) and pressure the backline while preparing Lucario Mega for a controlled late-game sweep. If Rotom’s Encore persists, plan to use Floette’s safer actions and preserve Lucario’s mega window for the final stretch.

Incineroar Protects to survive potential Petal Blizzard or Brick Break. Protecting both ensures Floette is KO'd next turn if it survives Turn 9.

KO threat now: Incineroar is the main blocker; Moonblast provides STAB; Grimmsnarl's Brick Break on Incineroar adds utility and helps break any remaining screens. Keep dual screens up for Lucario Mega endgame. Floette cannot Mega Evolve this turn.

Garchomp Earthquake hits Rotom (2x) and Grimmsnarl (1x) for max damage. Protect has 50% fail chance risking Manectric death.

Hex KO on Manectric secures a 2v2 path, while Reflect refreshes your dual-screen chemistry to support Mega Lucario’s setup sweep. This preserves momentum and minimizes exposure to Earthquake damage from Garchomp while maintaining protection for Lucario's imminent role.

Protect preserves Incineroar for next turn while Garchomp chips Grimmsnarl. Flare Blitz risks fainting Incineroar from recoil. Fake Out risks flinch from Grimmsnarl if it's faster.

reflections.summary: Lost due to team-preview mismatch: Garchomp Choice Scarf was locked into Earthquake against Rotom Levitate, rendering it useless while Rotom chipped it down. The team lacked a Mega option to counter Floette-Eternal's priority.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Garchomp Scarf with a Ground-immune pivot or non-locked Garchomp to handle Rotom; consider bringing a Mega Manectric to counter Floette-Eternal's priority.
reflections.notebook: Opponent Floette-Eternal holds Floettite (Mega priority threat). Opponent Rotom is a primary pivot with Levitate immunity to Ground. Opponent Grimmsnarl uses Light Clay screens + Prankster. Opponent Dragapult Scarf is a late-game threat. Opponent Absol Focus Sash revenge killer. Plan: Avoid Garchomp Scarf vs Rotom matchup. Plan: Bring Mega Manectric to counter Floette.

reflections.summary: The game swung on Rotom’s late-game Hex finishing Garchomp. Grimmsnarl and Gholdengo were knocked out early, leaving Rotom to carry a narrow win condition that only materialized when Garchomp, burn-affected and later locked into Earthquake by a Choice-Scarf, fell to a critical Hex. The intended Mega Lucario did not enter the field to pressure earlier or provide screens, so the preview plan didn’t convert into a timely win.
reflections.adjustment: Bring and Mega-evolve Lucario in game 3 (instead of relying on Floette-Eternal) to apply early offensive pressure and provide additional protection via Screens, aligning with the plan to gate Lucario for a win condition while Rotom chips away.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies observed: Garchomp is Choice-Scarf and Brn, frequently pressured Rotom with Earthquake; Rotom can set up Will-O-Wisp and Hex to wear down walls; Whimsicott-like backline presence (though not directly used for Tailwind in this game) suggests speed control and sashes are common; The Mega plan with Lucario was intended but not executed, leaving Rotom as the sole late-game finisher. Future plans: field Lucario Mega earlier to disrupt the opponent’s endgame tempo, preserve Rotom with screens, and ensure a concrete win condition before the opponent’s offensive pivots. Also consider bench options to maintain offensive pressure if Grimmsnarl/Gholdengo falter early.
